statement: HIF-1 (hypoxia-inducible factor) is the master transcription factor by which cells sense oxygen: under hypoxia it is stabilized and drives erythropoietin, VEGF/angiogenesis, glycolytic enzymes and metabolic reprogramming; under normoxia it is degraded via prolyl-hydroxylase/VHL.
effect_size: Foundational pathway; the oxygen-homeostasis switch (Nobel Prize 2019)

provenance.primary: Semenza & Wang - 'A nuclear factor induced by hypoxia via de novo protein synthesis binds to the human erythropoietin gene enhancer at a site required for transcriptional activation', Molecular and Cellular Biology 1992
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: FOUNDATION-grade mechanism (Kaelin/Ratcliffe/Semenza, Nobel 2019). Canon-promotion candidate. Being Nobel-grade does NOT license any downstream hypoxia longevity protocol - that is the strict mechanism->outcome firewall for this domain.

statement: EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) shows the strongest signal of recent natural selection distinguishing high-altitude Tibetans from lowland Han Chinese - among the most extreme allele-frequency differences known between human populations.
effect_size: EPAS1 = top genome-wide selection signal in Tibetans (extreme Fst vs Han)

provenance.primary: Yi et al. - 'Sequencing of 50 Human Exomes Reveals Adaptation to High Altitude', Science 2010
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Genetic mechanism, not an outcome. Demonstrates HIF-pathway adaptation to chronic hypoxia - says nothing about hypoxia CAUSING longevity. Different populations (Andean, Ethiopian) adapted differently: no single altitude-gene-longevity story.

statement: Independent evidence confirms EPAS1 and EGLN1 (the prolyl-hydroxylase that targets HIF for degradation) are under positive selection in Tibetans - converging on the HIF oxygen-sensing axis as the adaptation locus.
effect_size: EPAS1 + EGLN1 selection signals in Tibetan highlanders

provenance.primary: Simonson et al. - 'Genetic Evidence for High-Altitude Adaptation in Tibet', Science 2010
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Replication of the EPAS1 finding plus EGLN1, both on the HIF axis. Genetic/cross-sectional mechanism.

statement: Tibetan EPAS1 variants associate with LOWER hemoglobin concentration at altitude - the adaptation is to tolerate chronic hypoxia WITHOUT maladaptive polycythemia, not to over-produce red blood cells.
effect_size: EPAS1 genotype associated with reduced hemoglobin in Tibetan highlanders

provenance.primary: Beall et al. - 'Natural selection on EPAS1 (HIF2alpha) associated with low hemoglobin concentration in Tibetan highlanders', PNAS 2010
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: The adaptive phenotype is the OPPOSITE of the naive 'more EPO/red cells' intuition - it avoids the Andean chronic-mountain-sickness polycythemia route. Anti-laundering: altitude adaptation = tolerating hypoxia, not a longevity mechanism.

statement: Higher residential altitude is associated with lower cardiovascular (CHD/stroke) and some-cause mortality in population cohorts - but the association is heavily confounded.
effect_size: Lower CHD and stroke mortality per ~1,000 m residential altitude (Swiss National Cohort)

provenance.primary: Faeh, Gutzwiller & Bopp (Swiss National Cohort) - 'Lower mortality from coronary heart disease and stroke at higher altitudes in Switzerland', Circulation 2009
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; DOI from established citation (OpenAlex auto-lookup rate-limited this session, not machine-verified)

confidence_notes: Most confounded cohort claim in the domain. Altitude correlates with lower obesity, more physical activity (terrain), cooler temperature, higher UV, diet, migration/healthy-mover selection, air quality. Direction real, CAUSE unknown; not attributable to hypoxia per se. MR on altitude infeasible. NOTE: DOI is from established knowledge; OpenAlex verification failed (rate limit), flagged honestly.

statement: Intermittent hypoxia is dose-dependent and bidirectional: low-dose (mild, few brief cycles/day) drives beneficial respiratory/motor/vascular/metabolic plasticity, while high-dose (severe, many cycles, as in obstructive sleep apnea) is pathological - hypertension, oxidative stress, cardiovascular and cognitive harm.
effect_size: Therapeutic plasticity at low dose; OSA-equivalent pathology at high dose - same stimulus, opposite outcomes by dose
population: Review of human + animal intermittent-hypoxia physiology

provenance.primary: Navarrete-Opazo & Mitchell - 'Therapeutic potential of intermittent hypoxia: a matter of dose', Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol 2014
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: The MOST important claim in the domain and the purest hormesis illustration in the corpus: identical intermittent hypoxia is therapeutic at low dose and the pathological engine of sleep apnea at high dose. Any 'hypoxic training' claim that omits dose is laundering. Cross-links Domain H (hormesis) and Domain I (OSA).

statement: Intermittent hypoxia-hyperoxia training (IHHT) in older adults reportedly improves exercise tolerance, body composition and some cognitive measures in small early trials.
effect_size: Improved exercise tolerance / cognitive / body-composition surrogates in small RCTs
population: Small RCTs in older / cardiometabolic-risk adults

provenance.primary: Body of small IHHT RCTs (e.g., Bayer/Glazachev/Behrendt groups); see Navarrete-Opazo & Mitchell 2014 framework (10.1152/ajpregu.00208.2014) for the dose rationale
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-5 domain build; specific trial DOIs not individually OpenAlex-verified this session

confidence_notes: Promising but small, short, surrogate-endpoint RCTs - NOT established outcome. Hard-endpoint trials in aging do not exist. Graded rct but flagged as low-power/surrogate; specific trial citations to be pinned in Wave 6.

statement: Repeated maximal breath-holds trigger splenic contraction, transiently raising circulating hematocrit and oxygen-carrying capacity - a genuine acute hematological adaptation, enhanced in trained freedivers.
effect_size: Acute spleen volume reduction with transient hematocrit rise across repeated apneas
population: Human apnea physiology (trained and untrained subjects)

provenance.primary: Bakovic et al. - 'Spleen volume and blood flow response to repeated breath-hold apneas', Journal of Applied Physiology 2003
provenance.surfaced_via: named in Wave-5 brief; OpenAlex direct-DOI verified

confidence_notes: Real mechanistic adaptation (spleen, plus transient EPO and improved chemoreflex tolerance over training). NOT evidence of healthspan extension. HARD SAFETY BOUNDARY: hypoxic breath-holds, especially near water, risk shallow-water blackout/drowning (cross-link Domain G / Wim Hof hazard).

statement: Altitude/hypoxic exposure for athletes ('live high, train low', altitude tents) improves erythropoietic and some endurance-performance markers, but this is a performance literature with no demonstrated transfer to longevity or healthspan.
effect_size: Improved EPO/erythropoietic and endurance-performance surrogates (performance, not health endpoints)

provenance.primary: Live-high-train-low athletic-performance literature (Levine & Stray-Gundersen lineage); indexed for completeness
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-5 domain build; performance-domain cross-reference (specific DOIs not pinned this session)

confidence_notes: Explicitly flagged: performance != healthspan. Indexed so the map is complete; the longevity transfer is unestablished. Cross-link Domain E (exercise).
